subject: Post-call recap: Acme - Cost / TCO discussion and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acme.com>, Priya Joshi <priya.joshi@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 13:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme - Cost / TCO discussion and next steps

Hi Sam and Priya -

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our side so we're all aligned and so you have the TCO assumptions in one place. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you shared:
- High per-request costs on your current provider with unpredictable spikes tied to prompt length and user session patterns.
- Need to keep latency under 300ms p50 for ticket triage flows.
- Regulatory requirement to limit customer data residency and have clear audit logs.

Goals we heard:
- Reduce inference spend by 30-50% without degrading quality (same model behavior).
- Maintain p50 latency <= 300ms for the most common routes; tolerate higher tail latency for low-priority batch jobs.
- Pilot on a subset of traffic (~20% of active users) within 8 weeks.

High-level TCO / token economics (initial estimate) - see attached workbook for line-by-line detail:
- Current baseline (your numbers): ~2M interactions/month, average interaction = 550 tokens (150 prompt / 400 completion) -> ~1.1B tokens/month.
- Current spend (your reported blended rate): ~$30k/month.

Redwood projected optimizations and impact:
1) Prefix/response caching: for repeat prompts and shared system prompts we expect 10-25% token reduction on completion side for triage flows.
2) Intelligent batching: increase GPU utilization on backend leading to 15-30% per-token compute reduction for higher-throughput routes.
3) Model/quantization profile: switching to a quantized variant for background/low-priority routes can reduce cost further ~20% with negligible quality impact for those paths.

Conservative combined estimate: 40% reduction in unit spend -> projected Redwood monthly cost ~ $18k (vs $30k today) = ~$12k/month savings.
Upside (aggressive) case: with targeted caching + batching + route segregation, 55% reduction -> ~$13.5k/month.

Next steps (agreed on call):
- Redwood to send detailed TCO workbook and example config (attached). (action: Marissa) - today
- Rafael to provide short note on latency/kv-cache behavior and recommended batching config for your triage route. (action: Rafael) - by Tue 2/24
- Acme to identify pilot dataset and a small set of test users (~5k monthly active) for an 8-week pilot. (action: Sam/Priya) - by Wed 2/25
- Schedule a technical onboarding call with your infra lead and our Private deployment PM if you want to scope VPC options. (action: Marissa/Monica) - propose timescales in reply

Attachments: redwood_tco_estimate_acme_v2.xlsx (cost model), redwood_benefit_summary.pdf (brief ROI bullets).

Thanks - looking forward to piloting this with you.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa - this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 
1) The 2M interactions/month number is our active sessions count; I'll confirm whether that maps to 2M API calls or fewer (we run some session-level batching today).
2) Latency constraint applies only to the web triage UI (the mobile path is less strict). p50 <= 300ms is the main SLA we care about.

I'll loop in infra on Wednesday and confirm pilot cohort by EOD Wed. Please make sure the workbook includes a line for our current CDN/edge costs so we can compare total end-to-end spend.

Also can Rafael confirm whether the caching numbers assume warm KV stores (i.e., running on Dedicated pools) or are achievable on hosted tier?

Sam

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme - Cost / TCO discussion and next steps

Great questions Sam - short technical note: 

- Caching assumptions: the 10-25% completion token reduction assumes that a meaningful portion of your triage prompts share system/preamble text and that we can maintain an in-memory KV cache on-serving nodes. On Redwood Hosted this is achievable with our managed cache (warm cache hit rates will be lower during cold-starts); Dedicated deployments with pinned pools will give higher sustained hit rates.

- Batching: the 15-30% compute reduction is due to larger batch sizes amortizing fixed kernel overhead and better GPU throughput; this depends on request concurrency. For the pilot (20% traffic), we expect modest batching gains initially (10-12%) and larger gains as you scale traffic or consolidate routes.

- Latency: we can keep p50 < 300ms for the triage route if you route higher-priority requests to a lower-batch/low-latency pool and send background jobs to batched pools. That's a standard routing policy; we can share an example routing config.

I'll attach a one-pager with the batching/cache config and a worked example for your 550-token profile. Also added a sample throughput curve so you can see how per-token cost drops as concurrency increases.

Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
